newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Key Australian report urges faster growth - paper.
newsitem.headline: Key Australian report urges faster growth - paper.

text.p: A report commissioned by the Australian government has urged the setting of a economic growth target of four percent or more and government incentives to increase growth, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said on Wednesday.

"The Federal Government has been urged to adopt a go-for-growth approach to running the economy, with an influential report to be released today recommending a formal target of four percent or more a year," the newspaper said.
The report, prepared by TNT Asia Pacific chief executive David Mortimer, urges the targeting of industry assistance, particularly tax concessions for research and development, the newspaper said.

The Mortimer report also recommends appointing an investment ambassador to "sell Australia" as an investment destination for foreign firms, and streamlining business assistance programmes to focus on exports and investment, it said.
The Australian newspaper said the report urged the use of special financial incentives to lure overseas investors into Australia rather than Asia.
"It argues a dramatic policy shift is necessary if Australia is to attract increased offshore investment at a time of intense international competition for capital," it said.

The recommendations, which follow a six month review of the conservative Liberal-National government's A$2 billion industry assistance programmes, will be handed to Industry Minister John Moore later on Wednesday.
